subject: Anesthesia
stem: A neonate needs intubation. The blade best suited is
explanation: Miller (straight) blade lifts the long, floppy epiglottis directly in infants. Macintosh is curved with its tip in the vallecula (adults).

subject: Anesthesia
stem: The tip of a Macintosh blade is placed in the
explanation: Indirect lift of the epiglottis through the hyoepiglottic ligament.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Post-dural puncture headache is least with which needle?
explanation: Pencil-point (Whitacre, Sprotte) separates dural fibres; Quincke cuts them. Tuohy/Crawford are epidural needles.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Identification of the epidural space is by
options: Loss of resistance to saline or air
explanation: Tuohy needle with loss-of-resistance (or hanging drop). CSF back-flow indicates dural puncture.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Which airway adjunct should not be used in a conscious patient?
explanation: It stimulates the gag reflex and may cause vomiting/laryngospasm; nasopharyngeal airway is better tolerated.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: A nasopharyngeal airway is relatively contraindicated in
explanation: Risk of intracranial insertion through a cribriform plate fracture; also avoid in coagulopathy and nasal trauma.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: The main disadvantage of a laryngeal mask airway is
explanation: It is supraglottic; the airway is not sealed against regurgitation. Contraindicated in full stomach; used as plan B in difficult airway.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Best confirmation of endotracheal tube placement is
explanation: Persistent EtCO2 waveform over several breaths; oesophageal intubation gives no sustained trace.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Which is the Jackson-Rees modification?
options: Ayre's T-piece with bag on the open limb (Mapleson F)
explanation: Mapleson F used in children <20 kg: low resistance and dead space; FGF 2–3 × minute ventilation.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: Mapleson A (Magill) circuit is most efficient during
explanation: Mapleson efficiency: spontaneous ventilation A > D = E > B = C; controlled ventilation D > B = C > A.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: A patient with carbon monoxide poisoning has SpO2 99%. The reason is
explanation: Two-wavelength oximetry cannot separate carboxy- from oxyhaemoglobin. Use co-oximetry for true saturation.

subject: Anesthesia
stem: In an adult, spinal needle insertion is done below
explanation: Adult conus medullaris ends at L1–L2; in children it ends at about L3, so insert lower.

subject: Surgery
stem: A clamp used to occlude bowel without crushing it is
explanation: Doyen is a non-crushing intestinal clamp. Kocher and Payr crush tissue (used on specimen side).

subject: Surgery
stem: Forceps used for holding the bowel, appendix or fallopian tube without damage are
explanation: Babcock has rounded, fenestrated atraumatic jaws. Allis has teeth and damages the structure; used on tissue to be removed.

subject: Surgery
stem: Sponge-holding forceps with ring-shaped jaws are
explanation: Rampley holds gauze for skin preparation and for holding the cervix.

subject: Surgery
stem: Which needle is used for bowel anastomosis?
explanation: Taper needles separate fibres without cutting, minimising leaks in bowel and vessels. Cutting needles are for skin and tough tissue.

subject: Surgery
stem: Which suture is non-absorbable monofilament with minimal reaction, used in vascular surgery?
explanation: Prolene is inert and non-absorbable; silk is braided with high reactivity.

subject: Surgery
stem: Polydioxanone (PDS) is
explanation: PDS retains tensile strength ~6 weeks and absorbs by ~180 days; used in abdominal wall closure.

subject: Surgery
stem: Veress needle for pneumoperitoneum is inserted at
explanation: Palmer's point (left subcostal, midclavicular) is used in obese or adhesions; pressure 12–15 mmHg.

subject: Surgery
stem: A patient with a pacemaker needs surgery; the safest cautery is
options: Monopolar with return pad on the thigh
explanation: Bipolar current passes only between the forceps tips, avoiding interference. Monopolar needs the return pad kept away from the heart.

subject: Surgery
stem: Harmonic scalpel works by
explanation: Ultrasonic energy denatures protein, sealing vessels up to ~5 mm with minimal lateral thermal spread.

subject: Surgery
stem: The Penrose drain functions by
explanation: Penrose is a soft latex passive drain; Redivac/JP are closed suction drains.

subject: Surgery
stem: A wire saw used for amputation of bone is
explanation: Gigli: flexible serrated wire passed around the bone with handles; Stryker is an oscillating power saw.

subject: Surgery
stem: The Satinsky clamp is used for
options: Partial occlusion of a large vessel
explanation: Curved vascular clamp that partially occludes IVC/aorta while flow continues.

subject: OBGY
stem: The forceps used for rotation in deep transverse arrest is
explanation: Kielland has minimal pelvic curve and sliding lock permitting rotation; Simpson cannot rotate safely.

subject: OBGY
stem: Which forceps are used for the aftercoming head in a breech?
explanation: Piper forceps have long shanks and a reverse pelvic curve to clear the baby's body.

subject: OBGY
stem: A ventouse is contraindicated in
explanation: Avoid <34 weeks (fragile skull, intraventricular haemorrhage risk), face/brow, bleeding disorders.

subject: OBGY
stem: The cup of a ventouse is applied over the
options: Flexion point 3 cm in front of the posterior fontanelle
explanation: Median flexion point (pivot) gives optimal flexion and traction axis.

subject: OBGY
stem: The speculum used in examination for genital prolapse is
explanation: Sims (duck-bill) retracts the posterior vaginal wall in left lateral (Sims) position; Cusco/Graves are bivalve for Pap.

subject: OBGY
stem: Cervical cytology samples are taken from
explanation: Ayre spatula for ectocervix at SCJ plus cytobrush for endocervical canal; fix immediately.

subject: OBGY
stem: Copper T 380A lasts
explanation: CuT 380A is licensed for 10 years; LNG-IUS 5 years (up to 8 in newer evidence); Multiload 375 5 years.

subject: OBGY
stem: The commonest cause for Copper T removal is
explanation: Menorrhagia and dysmenorrhoea are the usual reasons for discontinuation; perforation ~1/1000.

subject: OBGY
stem: Manual vacuum aspiration uses
explanation: MVA is suitable up to 12 weeks (WHO). Karman cannula 4–12 mm connected to a 60 mL syringe.

subject: OBGY
stem: The normal length of the uterine cavity measured by sound is
explanation: Normal sounding length 6–8 cm; <5 cm suggests Asherman or hypoplasia.

subject: OBGY
stem: The commonest episiotomy is
explanation: Mediolateral begins at fourchette and goes 60° away from midline (right) with scissors; midline has more third/fourth degree tears.

subject: OBGY
stem: FHR monitoring in labour uses
explanation: External CTG: Doppler ultrasound for FHR and strain gauge (toco) for contractions; internal scalp electrode is invasive alternative.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: The gold standard for IOP measurement is
explanation: Goldmann (Imbert-Fick law) applanates a 3.06 mm area; used with fluorescein and a slit lamp.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Schiotz tonometry reads falsely low in
explanation: Low scleral rigidity in high myopia lets the plunger indent more. Thick sclera reads high.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: The image on direct ophthalmoscopy is
explanation: Indirect ophthalmoscopy gives inverted real image (×4–5) with a wide field.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: To distinguish open from closed angle glaucoma, use
explanation: Gonioscopy visualises the iridocorneal angle (Shaffer / Spaeth grading).

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Humphrey visual field is an example of
explanation: Static threshold testing; Goldmann is manual kinetic perimetry with isopters.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: The retinoscope gives
explanation: Streak retinoscopy neutralises reflex movement with lenses to find refractive error.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: The instrument used for probing a congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction is
explanation: Probing at 6–12 months after failed massage; Bowman lacrimal probe sizes 0000–2.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Axial length for IOL power calculation is obtained by
explanation: A-scan applanation or immersion biometry; partial coherence interferometry is more precise.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Dense cataract obscures the fundus; to rule out retinal detachment use
explanation: B-scan sees through opaque media: detachment, vitreous haemorrhage, tumours.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Keratometer measures
explanation: Normal central K ≈ 43 D; astigmatism and IOL power.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Fluorescein angiography uses excitation by
options: Blue light (490 nm) and yellow-green filters
explanation: Sodium fluorescein is excited by blue and emits green-yellow (520–530 nm); ICG uses near-infrared.

subject: Ophthalmology
stem: Phacoemulsification uses ultrasonic frequency of about
explanation: Titanium needle vibrating at ~40 kHz emulsifies the nucleus via 2.2–3 mm incision.

subject: ENT
stem: The tuning fork usually used for clinical hearing tests is
explanation: 512 Hz gives least overtones and decays slowly enough; 128 Hz for vibration sense.

subject: ENT
stem: In sensorineural hearing loss of the right ear Weber lateralises to
explanation: Conductive loss lateralises to the affected ear; SNHL to the better ear.

subject: ENT
stem: Anterior rhinoscopy is performed with
explanation: Killian is longer, for septal surgery; Siegle is ear (pneumatic).

subject: ENT
stem: Elective tracheostomy is made at the
explanation: Avoid first ring (stenosis) and above the isthmus (cricoid injury).

subject: ENT
stem: The mouth gag used is
explanation: Boyle-Davis tongue blade with slot, held by Draffin rods.

subject: ENT
stem: The Siegle speculum is used to assess
explanation: Pneumatic otoscopy: positive/negative pressure; reduced mobility = middle ear effusion.

subject: ENT
stem: Best instrument to remove a round foreign body from a child's nose is
explanation: A hook passed beyond the object and pulled forward; forceps may push it back into the nasopharynx.

subject: ENT
stem: Foreign body bronchus in children is best removed by
explanation: Rigid bronchoscopy permits airway control and large forceps.

subject: ENT
stem: Wax removal tool with a loop is
explanation: Jobson Horne has a ring curette at one end and a cotton-wool carrier at the other.

subject: ENT
stem: Nasal bone fracture reduction uses
explanation: Walsham (with Asch for septum) reduces nasal fractures within 7–10 days.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Splint used for first-aid of a femoral shaft fracture is
explanation: Thomas splint with Pearson knee flexion supports and traction reduces pain and bleeding.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Radial nerve palsy (wrist drop) splint is
explanation: Dorsal cock-up (wrist extension) splint keeps the wrist from flexing.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Treatment of DDH at 3 months is
explanation: Pavlik harness up to 6 months; after that closed reduction and spica.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Maintenance after Ponseti casting uses
explanation: Boots-and-bar abduction brace 23 h/day for 3 months then at night until age 4.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Milwaukee brace is for curves with apex
explanation: Boston TLSO for apex below T7; Milwaukee CTLSO has a neck ring.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The circular external fixator used for limb lengthening is
explanation: Ilizarov (tensioned wires, distraction osteogenesis at 1 mm/day) vs Hoffmann (unilateral).

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A displaced femoral neck fracture in an elderly patient is treated by
explanation: Displaced neck of femur >65: arthroplasty; DHS/gamma nail are for intertrochanteric fractures.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Plaster of paris sets in
explanation: Plaster is exothermic; avoid hot water; limb weight-bearing after 24–48 h.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The instrument used to curette a bone cavity is
explanation: Volkmann spoon is a sharp curette used for debridement of bone cysts and abscess.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A smooth thin pin for fixing small bone fractures is
explanation: K-wires ≤ 2.2 mm; Steinmann is thicker for skeletal traction.

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Maximum safe continuous tourniquet time is
explanation: Upper limb pressure ~250 mmHg, lower limb ~300–350; release after 2 h.

subject: Radiology
stem: Best personnel monitoring device for radiation workers is
explanation: TLD (LiF) and film badges integrate dose; GM counters are for surveys/contamination.

subject: Radiology
stem: SI unit of absorbed radiation dose is
explanation: Gray = J/kg; sievert is equivalent/effective dose; becquerel is activity.

subject: Radiology
stem: The anode of an X-ray tube is made of
explanation: High melting point (3,410 °C) and high atomic number; rotating anode dissipates heat.

subject: Radiology
stem: The radionuclide commonly used in PET imaging is
explanation: F-18 FDG, positron emitter; Tc-99m is gamma (SPECT/planar).

subject: Radiology
stem: Half-life of technetium-99m is
explanation: Tc-99m emits 140 keV gamma; I-131 has 8-day half-life.

subject: Radiology
stem: Maximum permissible whole-body dose for radiation worker per year (average, ICRP/AERB) is
explanation: 20 mSv per year averaged over 5 years, not >30 mSv in any year.

subject: Radiology
stem: Source commonly used for HDR brachytherapy of cervix is
explanation: Ir-192 HDR afterloading; Cs-137 for LDR historically.

subject: Radiology
stem: The ultrasound probe works by
explanation: PZT crystal converts electrical energy to sound and back.

subject: Radiology
stem: MRI is contraindicated with
options: Cochlear implant (older devices) or ferromagnetic aneurysm clip
explanation: Ferromagnetic aneurysm clips, cochlear implants and older pacemakers; titanium implants are MR-safe.

subject: Radiology
stem: T-score of -2.7 at the hip indicates
explanation: T ≤ -2.5 osteoporosis; -1 to -2.5 osteopenia.

subject: Radiology
stem: Radiation exposure from a source is reduced most by
explanation: Doubling distance quarters dose; combine time, distance, shielding.

subject: Surgery
stem: Foley catheter balloon is inflated with
explanation: Saline may crystallise and block deflation; water is used (5–10 mL).

subject: Surgery
stem: After TURP, continuous irrigation requires a
explanation: The third channel carries irrigation fluid to clear clots.

subject: Surgery
stem: Tube used to control bleeding from oesophageal varices is
explanation: Gastric and oesophageal balloons; Minnesota tube adds an oesophageal aspiration port.

subject: Surgery
stem: The T-tube is placed in the
explanation: Drains bile after CBD exploration; T-tube cholangiogram done before removal.

subject: Surgery
stem: The safe triangle for chest drain insertion is bounded by
options: Lateral border of pectoralis major, anterior border of latissimus dorsi, and 5th ICS
Anterior superior iliac spine, pubic tubercle, inguinal ligament
explanation: Apex below axilla, 4th–5th ICS, anterior to mid-axillary line.

subject: Surgery
stem: Catheterisation is contraindicated in
explanation: Do retrograde urethrography first; suprapubic catheter if retention persists.

subject: Surgery
stem: A catheter of size 18 Fr has an external diameter of
explanation: Fr/3 = diameter in mm.

subject: Surgery
stem: The commonest cystoscope lens is
explanation: 0° for urethra, 30° bladder, 70° for anterior wall/neck.

subject: Surgery
stem: TURP syndrome is caused by absorption of
explanation: Hyponatraemia, hypervolaemia, visual disturbances; use bipolar saline TURP to avoid.

subject: Surgery
stem: Best bedside check for correct NG tube position is
explanation: NPSA/NHS: pH ≤5.5 or X-ray; auscultation unreliable.

subject: Surgery
stem: Double-J stent is placed in the
explanation: Maintains ureteric patency after endourology or in obstruction.

subject: Surgery
stem: Mushroom-tipped suprapubic catheter is the
explanation: Pezzer and Malecot are used for suprapubic cystostomy and nephrostomy.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Marsh test is used to detect
explanation: Arsenic converted to arsine; Reinsch test uses a copper strip.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Confirmatory test for blood is
explanation: Teichmann haemin crystals and Takayama haemochromogen crystals are confirmatory; Kastle-Meyer, benzidine, luminol are presumptive.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Test for seminal fluid based on choline is
explanation: Florence: iodine-potassium iodide gives brown choline periodide crystals; Barberio picric acid with spermine gives yellow needles.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Diatom test is done on
explanation: Diatoms in distant organs/bone marrow support antemortem drowning in freshwater.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Lowenstein-Jensen medium is used for
explanation: Egg-based with malachite green; 6–8 weeks growth.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: TCBS agar is selective for
explanation: V. cholerae gives yellow colonies on TCBS (sucrose fermenter).

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Autoclave at 121 °C needs pressure of
explanation: 121 °C at 15 psi for 15 minutes; 134 °C 30 psi 3 minutes.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Class II biosafety cabinet uses
explanation: Protects worker, sample and environment; class III is a glove box for BSL-4.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Loeffler's serum slope is used to grow
explanation: Metachromatic granules visible with Albert stain.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Anaerobic jar uses
explanation: Palladium combines H2 and O2 to remove oxygen; GasPak generates H2 and CO2.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Alcohol breath analysers rely on a breath:blood ratio of
explanation: Henry's law; partition ratio 2100:1.

subject: Forensic Medicine
stem: Intraoperative frozen sections are cut on
explanation: Frozen tissue sectioned at −20 °C and stained with H&E in ~15 minutes.
